title: Extract CI step factory and optimize dependency-update pathing
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: our CI pipelines have accumulated ad-hoc step definitions across multiple workflows and the dependency-updater path (staging->release) had redundant network calls and brittle retry logic. This PR extracts a small, testable "CI step factory" library that standardizes step metadata, retry/backoff behavior, and artifact pinning, and it centralizes dep-update orchestration to remove duplicate fetches and tighten gating. Changes include: 1) new package ci/stepfactory (Go) with a light DSL for defining reusable GitHub Actions and composite steps; 2) action/workflow updates to consume the factory (ci/workflows/*) and remove duplicated matrix/step wiring; 3) refactor of tools/dep-updater to introduce an idempotent, cached fetch stage and a resumable update transaction; 4) small ergonomics improvements to the release runner to expose explicit stage markers for telemetry. The description below summarizes commits, changed areas, CI run summary, and review conversation. This PR is intended to be non-breaking for teams consuming our actions; most callers opt in by switching to the new composite steps. Rollout plan: land on main behind feature flag workflows.ci_factory_enabled=false, flip traffic in a staged manner across repos over one week, monitor presubmit flake count and merge latency metrics. Backwards compatibility: the old composite action remains in place for 48 hours and a migration guide was added. Related: ENG-4012 (ci hygiene), ENG-4080 (dep-update reliability).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice decomposition. Two asks: 1) add a short benchmark for factory startup in unit tests to ensure we don't regress action runtime, 2) consider moving the fetch cache TTL into configuration so infra teams can tune it. Response (Aisha): added micro-benchmark and made TTL overrideable via DEP_UPDATER_CACHE_TTL env var.

Sofia Martinez: The resumable transaction model is good but can we add a guard so an interrupted run never leaves a half-updated lock file? Suggestion: write a transaction manifest to tmp and atomically swap. Response (Aisha): implemented transaction manifest + atomic replace, added unit test that simulates SIGTERM.

Ethan Zhou: CI workflow diffs look smaller — can you list which repositories we plan to flip first and what the monitoring thresholds are? Response (Aisha): added rollout plan to docs/migration/ci-step-factory.md and a small script scripts/feature_gate/flip-ci-factory.sh; proposed first wave: redwood, redwood-docs, redwood-examples; monitoring thresholds: presubmit flake delta <2% and median presubmit time change <150ms.

release_notes: Centralize CI step definitions into a reusable stepfactory, optimize dependency updater path with cached fetch and resumable transactions, add migration guide and feature-flag for staged rollout.
merge_outcome_notes: Merged after two approvals and a green CI run. Feature-flag left disabled by default; ops to flip across first-wave repos on 2025-02-20 pending post-merge telemetry checks.
